answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing paid tasks whose outputs are checked against hidden test cases and later audited by randomly selected peers. A mesa of reviewers can reject copied or coordinated work, while a grove of independent clients funds tasks and a gale of new identities cannot multiply the same scarce review capacity. Each accepted identity therefore requires real labor, stake at risk for fraud, and time to build a track record; fabricating a crowd costs more than creating accounts.
